result:
Parking the roadmap. Since there are no methodology or critique files, nothing else retires with it. Here are the calls, in order:

**1. Read the schema and the current backlog**

```
Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/references/deferred-backlog.md   # Deferred-item schema
Read specs/deferred_items.md                                          # may not exist yet
```

**2. Append to `specs/deferred_items.md`**

There is one item for the unticked stage and one for each Ranked-list item. The fields below will be fitted to the schema from step 1.

```markdown
## lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06

- [ ] Closure-notice emails to boat operators (was Stage 2, Track B, outcome O5).
      Email every boat operator on a mailing list within an hour of a lock closing,
      driven by the closure log's live feed. Parked when the canal study's funding ended.
      Size: small (one closure-log poll every 10 minutes).
      Done when: the notice job and its operator mailing list exist, and in a test an
      email reaches every address on the list within an hour of a new closure entry.

- [ ] 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock (was Track A Ranked list #1, outcome O2).
      Apply the closure-vs-gauge-level curve (specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md:
      steep rise above 3.1 m) to the river-level forecast, giving a daily 7-day risk
      for each lock. Parked when the canal study's funding ended.
      Size: small (one model run a day; Stage 1's fit took 22 min on a laptop).
      Done when: a 7-day closure-risk outlook for each lock is produced from a real
      river-level forecast.

- [ ] Pooled per-lock closure curves for all 14 locks (was Track A Ranked list #2, outcome O3).
      Fit separate closure-vs-gauge-level curves for each of the 14 locks, pooled across
      locks. Stage 1 found the four longest-record locks share nearly the same curve.
      Parked when the canal study's funding ended.
      Size: medium (about 14× Stage 1's data, roughly 25 GB, from 1.8 GB per Stage 1).
      Done when: a closure curve for each of the 14 locks, fit on the real closure log
      and gauge readings, is written up with the run's measured cost.

- [ ] Closure-history map for boat operators (was Track A Ranked list #3, outcome O4).
      A static map page showing each lock's closure history for the canal's boat
      operators. Parked when the canal study's funding ended.
      Size: about a day of work (one static map page).
      Done when: boat operators can open a map page showing each lock's closure history.
```

**3. Mark and move the roadmap**

Add this line under the title of `specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md`:

```
> PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete. Funding ended; remaining stage and Track A's Ranked list moved to specs/deferred_items.md.
```

Then move it and commit:

```
git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap (1 of 2 stages complete): funding ended"
```

**What stays put:** `specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md` stays in `specs/`. It is the only finished result, and the parked O2 and O3 items point to it.

**One gap:** Stage 2's `Leaves out` named text-message notices, but no stage or list item picked them up. They aren't a stage or a list item, so I haven't parked them. Tell me if you want a deferred item for them too.

Once these calls run, the roadmap is parked. There is no next stage to hand off.
